_what: Commands the catalog documents for USERS that no non-admin role can actually run.
_why: Each is either a catalog error (the command really is operator-only) or a permission error (users should be able to run it). Both readings are plausible per command and the fix differs, so they are recorded rather than guessed at. This is a RATCHET: new drift fails the test, the known backlog does not.
_fix: Move it to an admin group, or grant the permission to the roles that should have it.
_cleared: EMPTY as of 2026-07-27. All sixteen were resolved, and the split was 10/6 — the guess either way would have been wrong for a third of them, which is why they were recorded instead of guessed at. CATALOG WAS WRONG (10): autoconfirm, calibration, crossasset, equitycurve, forcescan, golive, journal, liveclose, montecarlo, strategy — each reads or mutates the SHARED operator engine (RUNTIME flags, engine.journal, engine.portfolio._history, the global risk engine and router), so the handler's refusal was right and the documentation was not. PERMISSION WAS WRONG (6): exposure, networth, research, rwa were invented at the @guard(...) decorator and never added to any role set, so the string existed and nobody held it while all four are read-only and caller-scoped or pure market data; buy and sell are inert stubs that print 'spot trading is disabled, use /trade' and were @guard('admin'), so a normal user typing /buy got silence — the exact 'commands feel broken' failure this catalogue exists to fix, on a command whose only job is to redirect them.
_do_not_refill: An entry added here is an accepted mismatch, not a TODO that gets done later — the ratchet stops complaining the moment it is listed. Fix the command instead, and add one only when the right fix genuinely cannot be decided yet.
